subject: Agriculture
title: What Is IPM?
description: A quick, practical guide to What Is IPM?.

hook.text: Integrated Pest Management uses every tool—biological, cultural, chemical—but pesticides only as a last resort.

buildup.text: IPM starts with monitoring. Farmers scout fields and only act when pest numbers cross an economic threshold.

discovery.text: Thresholds prevent unnecessary spraying. A few aphids aren't worth treating—only outbreaks justify chemical response.

twist.text: Indonesia banned 57 insecticides on rice in 1986 and adopted IPM. Rice yields actually increased.

climax.text: IPM works but requires knowledge and patience. Pesticide companies market simplicity—spray and forget.

punchline.text: The best pest management isn't one tool. It's all tools, in the right order.

quiz.question: What happened when Indonesia banned 57 insecticides and adopted IPM for rice?

details.summary: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) is a holistic approach that combines biological, cultural, mechanical, and chemical tools to manage pests with minimum economic, health, and environmental risk. It prioritizes prevention and uses pesticides only as a last resort.
details.whyItMatters: IPM is recognized by the FAO, WHO, and EPA as the gold standard for pest management. It reduces pesticide use by 50-70% while maintaining crop protection, benefiting farmer health, ecosystems, and consumer safety.
takeaways: IPM uses multiple tactics—biological, cultural, mechanical, and chemical—in combination
Monitoring and economic thresholds determine when intervention is actually necessary
IPM reduces pesticide use by 50-70% while maintaining effective crop protection

faq.question: What are the core principles of integrated pest management?
faq.answer: IPM starts with prevention through resistant varieties, crop rotation, and habitat management. Regular monitoring tracks pest levels. Action thresholds determine when intervention is needed. When control is required, biological and cultural methods are tried first, with chemicals as a last resort.

faq.question: How does IPM determine when to use pesticides?
faq.answer: IPM uses economic thresholds—the pest population level at which damage costs exceed control costs. Farmers monitor fields regularly and only spray when thresholds are exceeded, rather than spraying preventively on a calendar schedule. This dramatically reduces unnecessary pesticide applications.
